question: What happens if you fall into a black hole?
short_answer: If you fall into a stellar-mass black hole, extreme tidal forces stretch your body vertically and compress it horizontally in a process called spaghettification before crossing the event horizon.
full_explanation: Near a compact black hole, the gravitational pull on your feet is dramatically higher than on your head due to inverse-square tidal gradients, breaking atomic bonds before reaching the singularity.
